title: Policy library v1 (KYC Judgment v1 contract C1; E-002, E-010). DRAFT for Authoring and RL Gym review
description: Every PM-approved rule of one Authoring project's policy library, with each rule's whole version chain. Authoring exports it; Studio's generator copies it word for word into the environment's policies collection and refuses a text whose SHA-256 differs; the RL Gym resolves conditions from it. Rule identity is the triple (rule_id, version, text_sha256): rule_id is Authoring's rule key (unique in the project, which export.project_id names), version is Authoring's approved version number, the same in Authoring, Studio, the RL Gym and every receipt. text_sha256 is lower-case hex SHA-256 of the version's text as UTF-8 bytes, exactly as served (no trimming or normalisation). Only approved versions appear: an AI draft no person has reviewed is never exported. The library is every approved rule of the project, distractors included, never filtered by the owner's mandatory selection, which stays a private expectation in Authoring and in the task's expectedRules. Versions are append-only: a change is the next version of the same rule, and earlier versions stay in the chain. Agent visibility: rule_id, version, supersedes, title, kind, issuer, jurisdiction, text and effective are what policy.read serves. condition, scope, exception conditions, derived_facts, source and approval are private reference data, because serving them would give the agent the applicability answer.

library_id.description: The Authoring project's library, stable across exports (for example kyc-judgment.library).

library_revision.description: Authoring's library revision. It increases with every approved change; an environment version pins one.

fact_catalog.description: The fact catalog (catalog_id@version) the conditions and derived facts are written over.

documents.description: The source documents the rules were extracted from, each pinned by the SHA-256 of its uploaded bytes.

derived_facts.description: Facts the case data never states, defined by a rule of this library (for example us_person from citizenship alone: under the CIP rule a U.S. person is a U.S. citizen, and residency, lawful permanent residence included, does not make one). A resolver computes them from the case's facts with the definition in force; they never appear in case data or registry cases.

jurisdiction.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country, optionally with an ISO 3166-2 subdivision: US, US-CA. California is US-CA; a bare CA would be Canada.

kind.description: official_text: a statute or regulation. bank_policy: the bank's own written policy or operating choices.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the document's bytes as uploaded to Authoring. For a captured document it equals capture.sha256.

capture.description: Where and when an official text was downloaded (owner, 25 Nov: the California document was downloaded from California sites). Required for official_text.

definition.description: For a boolean fact: true exactly when this predicate holds over the catalog's facts.

scope.description: Review and filtering metadata only. Applicability comes from the condition alone: a rule from another process (for example currency transaction reporting) carries a condition on the process fact, so it never applies to this project's cases.

process.description: The same values as the fact catalog's process fact.

product_lines.description: Expert, 25 Nov: the SOP covers deposit accounts only; loan, credit card and mortgage rules are distractors. The same values as the fact catalog's product_line fact.

kind.description: The same enum as template.v1 policies.rules[].kind.

subject.description: What the condition is evaluated for. party: once per party, with that party's facts and the case's facts; the rule applies to the case when it applies to any party. case: once, with the case's facts.

versions.description: Every approved version, oldest first, with Authoring's own version numbers: strictly increasing, gaps allowed (an unreviewed draft or a collapsed duplicate takes a number but never appears). The first entry supersedes nothing; every later entry supersedes the entry before it.

supersedes.description: The version of the entry before this one in the chain.

change.description: How this version differs from the one it supersedes (for review and grading; never served).

text.description: The approved wording, served to the agent verbatim.

effect.description: obligation: the text imposes a requirement when the condition holds. withdrawn: from this version on the rule imposes nothing (its text says so).

condition.description: When the rule applies (clause-condition.v1, three-valued). null: wherever the project's approved scope applies (clause-condition.v1). For a fact whose catalog cardinality is many (citizenship, document_kinds), eq and in hold when any value matches; ne and not_in hold when none does.

effective.description: from_date: in force from that date. Without a scenario event, the version in force for a case is the latest from_date version whose date is on or before the case's submission date (applications.submitted_at). scenario_only: never in force at the start of an episode; only a scenario-event.v1 publication puts it in force.

quote.description: The source passage the text was extracted from, word for word.

approval.description: A person (the PM or policy owner) approved this version's text and condition. AI suggestions are never approval.
